extracted.intended_audience: patent valuation researchers, IP analysts, economists, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Framework for ex ante estimation of US patent value using owner and patent-characteristic signals (ownership type, litigation, citations, renewals, family scope). Intended to guide multi-signal quality/valuation judgments rather than doctrinal/legal analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner-Size Premium / Owner Type
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents issued to large corporations are substantially more valuable than patents issued to small entities; owner type (large corp, small entity, individual/NPE) signals baseline value and commercialization/enforcement capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use owner type as a primary baseline signal: large corporate owners indicate higher commercialization probability, stronger litigation/enforcement resources, and complementary assets; small entities indicate lower commercialization capacity and weaker enforcement (often licensing-focused); individual/NPE owners have variable value and require assessment on patent merits rather than presumed commercial use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation History (Litigation-Value Correlation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents that are litigated are systematically more valuable than non-litigated patents; litigation-tested validity (and survival) is a strong quality/value signal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat survived litigation as a strong positive signal. Consider IPR survival as a lighter-weight but similar signal. Multiple successful litigations against different defendants increase the strength of the signal. Note causation may run both ways (valuable patents are more likely to be litigated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward Citations (Citation-Value Correlation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Highly cited patents tend to be more valuable, but citations explain only a small fraction of value variance—citations are useful but limited as standalone quality measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use citation counts in combination with other indicators; value improves if citations come from diverse firms. Prefer multi-indicator approaches (e.g., Lanjouw-Schankerman, OECD style) over citation-only measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal Pattern / Maintenance Fee Payments (Revealed-Preference Signal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance/renewal decisions reveal owner expectations of value. Paying maintenance fees at years 4, 8, and 12 indicates progressively stronger revealed-preference value (year 12 = full-term commitment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret year-4 payment as belief in near-term commercial value, year-8 as moderate commitment, year-12 as full-term high commitment. Patents abandoned at year 4 or 8 are revealed to have low revealed-preference value. Account for small-entity fee discounts when interpreting renewals.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Family / Triadic Family Scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The geographic scope of the patent family signals commercial intent; triadic/international families covering major markets indicate higher value than US-only families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat triadic/international family coverage as a strong positive indicator of commercial belief and expected market importance; US-only families are weaker markers of value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operative Quality Markers (Strong vs Weak)
rubrics_metrics.description: A synthesized list of strong and weak markers that together identify high- versus low-value patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong markers: large corporate owner with commercial activity; patent litigated and survived; multiple forward citations across diverse firms; renewed through full term; international (triadic) family. Weak markers: small or individual owner with no commercial activity; never litigated; few/no forward citations; abandoned at first/second maintenance fee; US-only family. Use the combination of these markers to rank expected value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-Indicator Integration Recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Single indicators (especially citations alone) are insufficient; combining ownership, behavioral, and technical signals outperforms citation-only approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate owner type, renewal behavior, litigation history, citation patterns, and family scope when estimating value. Reference multi-indicator frameworks (Lanjouw-Schankerman, OECD) as superior to citation-only measures; include renewal patterns to capture what citations miss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confounders and Limitations to Interpret Signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Several factors can distort the value signals: small-entity fee discounts, cash-constrained firms abandoning valuable patents, defensive renewals, and standard-essential patents renewed for licensing pool participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust interpretation to account for confounders: check for small-entity status (fee discounts), firm financial constraints, defensive portfolio strategies, and SEP/licensing context when using renewals or ownership as signals. Recognize that litigation presence correlates with value but may reflect strategic behavior.
